title: Senior system design + applied AI exam
description: Design a multi-tenant enterprise assistant, then adapt it to seven sequential incidents. All engineering judgments need review.

questions.prompt: Serve 300 companies, 2 million source documents and 5,000 daily users. Define personas, tenant/role boundaries, freshness, availability, latency, cost and explicit non-goals. Show assumptions and capacity arithmetic.
questions.title: Requirements and workload

questions.prompt: Describe modules, API examples, database keys/indexes, cache keys, queues, idempotency, ingestion/version replacement, hybrid retrieval/reranking and citation paths. Give the main sequence and failure boundaries.
questions.title: Architecture and contracts

questions.prompt: Explain actor-derived scope, document ACL changes, citation rechecks, strict tool schemas, action-bound approvals, replay/reconciliation and audit records. Model and document text never acquire mutation authority.
questions.title: Permissions and trusted actions

questions.prompt: Specify held-out retrieval/answer evaluation, human review, budgets, safe observability, rollout/rollback, scaling, backups, restore, RPO/RTO and costs. Include tests and residual risks.
questions.title: Quality, deployment and recovery
Traffic increased 20×
questions.prompt: Tenant adoption grows 20× in one week. The average document is 20 KB. Your prior latency/cost budget stays fixed. Recalculate capacity, admission/backpressure, isolation and a measured scaling experiment.

questions.title: PostgreSQL is overloaded
questions.prompt: p99 read latency doubles and connections saturate during ingestion. Identify measurements, query/transaction/pool changes, workload isolation and correctness risks. Explain how to verify the change.

questions.title: Redis is unavailable
questions.prompt: The cache/broker service is unavailable for 15 minutes. Preserve authorization and prevent a retry storm. State what works, what degrades, recovery and observable acceptance criteria.

questions.title: Model provider outage
questions.prompt: The model provider fails for 30 seconds while an approved action may already have committed. Explain budgets, user response, receipt reconciliation and how to avoid a duplicate mutation.

questions.title: Attacker uploads instructions
questions.prompt: A permitted source includes instructions to export another tenant’s private data. Trace its trust boundary through retrieval, model output, tool proposals and citations. Provide attack tests and residual semantic risk.

questions.title: A tool was executed twice
questions.prompt: The tool destination charged twice even though your local inbox has one row. Explain the protection boundary, evidence collection, reconciliation/compensation and a changed destination contract.

questions.title: Retrieval returns irrelevant documents
questions.prompt: Recall on the held-out multilingual set falls after re-embedding. Diagnose model/version, labels, ACL, source freshness, chunking and reranking without tuning away the held-out evidence. Define release criteria.

rubric.title: Explicit requirements and capacity
rubric.expectation: State measurable SLOs, workload arithmetic, tenant assumptions, non-goals and changing limits.

rubric.title: Data and service design
rubric.expectation: Show full keys/indexes, API contracts, write ownership, caching/queues and justified trade-offs.

rubric.title: Permissions and action authority
rubric.expectation: Enforce current ACLs at every exposure, strict tools and exact action approval; include adversarial tests.

rubric.title: Failures and durable effects
rubric.expectation: Reason about commit/ack gaps, destination cooperation, retries, fallback, duplicate receipts and uncertain outcomes.

rubric.title: Retrieval and semantic quality
rubric.expectation: Preserve sources/versions/citations, measured hybrid retrieval and held-out labels, independent human quality checks.

rubric.title: Operations, recovery and cost
rubric.expectation: Give safe traces, budgets, deploy/rollback, restore drills and concrete RPO/RTO/SLO evidence.

rubric.title: Incident adaptation
rubric.expectation: For each incident revise earlier assumptions, choose a response, explain trade-offs and define a verification experiment.
